reason: 'Margin rolled under' means revolute. It is said of the leaf margin.
The seeds narrow toward the base, so 'seed tapered' is true. The base position is left out, but leaving it out does not make the statement false.
In FNA, 'Plants a × b dm' gives height × spread. So 1-3 dm = 10-30 cm is the height of the whole plant, and the unit is converted correctly.
'Seta flexuose, 2 mm' is the length of the moss seta (PO_0030032).
About 3 secondary veins on each side of the midvein (PO_0020139), counted in the leaf blade. 'ca.' only makes the number approximate.
'Shrub or small tree' gives two habit alternatives for the whole plant: frutescent and arborescent.
The scales of the spike are bracts, and 'erose-fimbriate' reads as a range from erose to fimbriate. The same words are also said of the sepals, but the bract reading fits the first occurrence.

fix: Pattern 'Stamens ...; filaments X': X belongs to the part named just before it (the filament), not to the part of the earlier sentence (the stamen).
reason: The flora calls the filaments subulate, not the whole stamen.
The leaf blades are glabrous at maturity. The 'mature' context (PATO_0001701) captures 'at least at maturity'.
'Inflorescence few-flowered' is a count word: flowers present in the inflorescence, amount 'few'.

fix: Pattern 'stalk ± N mm long': this is a measured length with a number, not 'increased length'. Also, in orchids the anther stalk is not a true filament, so the bearer is doubtful too.
reason: The flora gives the stalk's length as about 2 mm. It does not say the stalk is long.

fix: A more specific bearer exists: caryopsis fruit (PO_0030104).
reason: 'Caryopsis ca. 1.8 mm' is the length of the fruit. 'Fruit' is true but more general than it needs to be.
In bamboos the culm sheath is a leaf sheath, and the flora calls the culm sheaths glabrous.
Oblanceolate and spathulate are two of the listed leaf-blade shape alternatives across the taxon.
'Obovate-elliptic' is a leaf-blade shape between obovate and elliptic.

fix: Pattern 'Floats ... on the scape, 5–7': this counts floats, which are specialised inflated organs on the scape. Without a float bearer, or at least the scape as the container, the count must not go to 'leaf'.
reason: 'Leaf amount 5–7' says the plant has 5–7 leaves. That is false: the plant has many leaves, and 5–7 is the number of floats.
The outermost leaf sheaths are greyish brown. The 'outer' context (FLOPO_0991379) captures 'outermost'.
The anthers are about 0.7 cm long.

target: grayish pale yellow OR greenish pale yellow (base: pale yellow, PATO_0001286)
fix: Pattern 'slightly A or B C-colour': 'A or B' are tints of the shared base colour C, so read it as (A C) or (B C). Do not split it as 'A' or 'B C'.
reason: The stigmas are pale yellow with a slight grey or green tinge. They are never just 'grayish', and the alternative should be greenish pale yellow, not greenish yellow.
Ripe seeds are 0.8-0.9 mm long, and the 'mature' context captures 'ripe'.
'Ovary globose, c. 1.5 mm diam., glabrous': the ovary is glabrous.
The terminal pinna is forked in its lower part. The 'terminal' context (PATO_0002476) keeps this from being said of the side pinnae.

fix: A more specific bearer exists: secondary leaf vein (PO_0020140), with the margin as the place.
reason: The secondary veins join up near the margins, so 'vascular bundle anastomosing' is true, if general.
'Glabrous above' on the leaflets means the upper (adaxial) side is glabrous.
'Nutant' means nodding, which is the drooping flower quality.
The spike is many-flowered: flowers present in the inflorescence, amount 'many'.

fix: The 'basal leaf' context would make it more precise.
reason: The leaf blade has 1-3 veins. This is said of the basal leaves, but the annotation is not false without that.

fix: Pattern 'Phyllaries ..., margins N mm wide': the width belongs to the margin (a narrow scarious band), not to the whole bract.
reason: 0–0.3 mm is the width of the phyllary margin. The phyllary itself is much wider.
The glomerules (flower clusters) become fleshy at the fruit stage, and the fruit-stage context captures 'in fruit'.
The leaf blade has 3 veins on each side.
